## AI Disclosure
Fable helped me track down and repro this issue. I reviewed the code myself. 

## Motivation

`--disable-overlap-schedule` is listed as a supported flag in the Apple Silicon docs, but on the MLX backend the server crashes on the first batch that contains two or more requests:

```
RuntimeError: Expected all tensors to be on the same device, but found at least two devices, mps:0 and cpu!
  File "sglang/srt/managers/scheduler.py", line 4480, in _relay_forward_payload
  File "sglang/srt/managers/overlap_utils.py", line 608, in stash
```

Repro on an M4 Pro:

```bash
SGLANG_USE_MLX=1 python -m sglang.launch_server --model-path Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B \
  --disable-cuda-graph --max-total-tokens 32768 --disable-overlap-schedule
# send the same prompt twice, or any two concurrent requests
```

**Root cause.** `Scheduler.init_overlap` creates the `FutureMap` on `self.device`, which is `"mps"` on MLX. But the MLX backend keeps `req_to_token_pool`, every `ScheduleBatch` tensor, and the worker's `next_token_ids` on CPU. `FutureMap.stash` does `output_tokens_buf[req_pool_indices] = next_token_ids` with CPU index and value tensors against an mps buffer. PyTorch tolerates a one-element CPU value there (the CPU-scalar exception), so single-request batches worked by accident, and the first two-request batch raised.

## Modifications

- `Scheduler.init_overlap`: pass `self.req_to_token_pool.device` to `create_future_map` instead of `self.device`. The `FutureMap` is indexed by `req_pool_idx` and only ever meets batch tensors, so the pool device is the correct one. On CUDA the two are the same device, so this is a no-op there.
- `test/registered/unit/hardware_backend/mlx/test_attention_patching.py`: extract the existing `init_overlap` scheduler setup into `_init_overlap_mlx_scheduler(device)` and add `test_mlx_scheduler_future_map_follows_req_pool_device`, which runs `init_overlap` with the scheduler device set to `"mps"` and stashes a two-row CPU payload. It fails with the error above without the fix and is skipped where MPS is unavailable.

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable, no change to model forward code. Verified on M4 Pro with Qwen3-0.6B.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable.

- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). Not applicable.

nodes.body: @yeahdongcn let me know if you want me to make any changes/test more, happy to help

Four PRs fix the same FutureMap.stash device mismatch: #36200, #39222, #39281, #43099. Measured on an M4 Pro: copying the payload to MPS per stash (#43099, #36200) blocks 25 ms when MLX work is in flight. Allocating the FutureMap on the pool device (#39222) keeps every write same device, under 0.1 ms; #39281 does the same behind a `use_mlx()` check.

Suggest landing #39222 with #43099’s test and closing the rest toward it.

Thanks for the comparison. I've pulled #43099's test into this PR (3efa26d) as `test/registered/unit/hardware_backend/mlx/test_overlap_stash_device.py`, registered in `stage-a-unit-test-mlx`.

I had to adapt it: the original builds `FutureMap` on `mps` directly and stashes a CPU payload, which only passes with #43099's `.to(device=...)` change. Here it runs `Scheduler.init_overlap` with an `mps` scheduler device and checks that the relay lands on the pool's CPU device and that an n=2 stash works. The mps-only test that was in `test_attention_patching.py` moved into the new file, so this test needs MPS but not mlx.

On an M-series Mac: 3/3 pass on this branch. With `init_overlap` reverted to `self.device`, the two stash tests fail with `Expected all tensors to be on the same device ... mps:0 and cpu`, and the n=1 sanity test still passes, as expected.

files.patch:
@@ -1693,8 +1693,13 @@ def init_overlap(self):
             attn_backends = (self.tp_worker.model_runner.attn_backend,)
         needs_cpu_seq_lens = decide_needs_cpu_seq_lens(attn_backends)
         needs_confidence_relay = decide_needs_confidence_relay()
+        # FutureMap bufs are indexed by req_pool_idx and written/read with
+        # batch tensors (req_pool_indices, next_token_ids, seq_lens), which
+        # live on the req_to_token_pool's device. On CUDA that is self.device;
+        # the MLX backend keeps its pools and batches on CPU while self.device
+        # is "mps", so the relay must follow the pool, not the accelerator.
         self.future_map = self.spec_algorithm.create_future_map(
-            self.device,
+            self.req_to_token_pool.device,
             self.req_to_token_pool,
             needs_cpu_seq_lens=needs_cpu_seq_lens,
             needs_confidence_relay=needs_confidence_relay,

@@ -0,0 +1,110 @@
+"""Regression tests for the MLX ``--disable-overlap-schedule`` crash.
+
+On MLX the scheduler's device is ``mps`` while the req_to_token_pool, every
+ScheduleBatch tensor and the stub worker's sampled tokens live on CPU.  With
+``--disable-overlap-schedule`` the scheduler still relays decode inputs
+through ``FutureMap.stash()``.  A FutureMap built on the scheduler's device
+put its relay buffers on ``mps``, and for batched scatters (n >= 2)
+``torch.index_put_`` requires the value and the buffer on the same device, so
+any concurrent decode batch crashed the scheduler (single-row n == 1 scatters
+hid the bug via index_put_'s single-element fast path).  The FutureMap must
+follow the req_to_token_pool's device instead.
+
+Adapted from the tests in #43099.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import platform
+import unittest
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+from unittest import mock
+
+import torch
+
+from sglang.srt.managers import scheduler as scheduler_module
+from sglang.srt.managers.overlap_utils import RelayPayload
+from sglang.srt.managers.scheduler import Scheduler
+from sglang.srt.mem_cache.memory_pool import ReqToTokenPool
+from sglang.srt.server_args import ServerArgs, set_global_server_args_for_scheduler
+from sglang.srt.speculative.spec_info import SpeculativeAlgorithm
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_mlx_ci
+
+register_mlx_ci(est_time=1, suite="stage-a-unit-test-mlx")
+
+_IS_APPLE_SILICON = platform.system() == "Darwin" and platform.machine() == "arm64"
+_SKIP_REASON = "requires Apple Silicon with an available MPS device"
+
+
+def _init_overlap_mlx_scheduler(device: str) -> Scheduler:
+    """Run ``Scheduler.init_overlap`` on a bare MLX-style scheduler.
+
+    ``device`` is the scheduler's accelerator device; the MLX backend keeps
+    ``req_to_token_pool`` on CPU regardless.
+    """
+    scheduler = object.__new__(Scheduler)
+    scheduler.device = device
+    scheduler.draft_worker = None
+    scheduler.tp_worker = SimpleNamespace(
+        model_runner=SimpleNamespace(attn_backend=None)
+    )
+    scheduler.server_args = SimpleNamespace(
+        enable_two_batch_overlap=False,
+        cuda_graph_config=None,
+        speculative_algorithm=None,
+    )
+    scheduler.spec_algorithm = SpeculativeAlgorithm.NONE
+    scheduler.req_to_token_pool = ReqToTokenPool(
+        size=8,
+        max_context_len=16,
+        device="cpu",
+        enable_memory_saver=False,
+    )
+    scheduler.enable_overlap = False
+
+    with mock.patch.object(scheduler_module, "use_mlx", lambda: True):
+        Scheduler.init_overlap(scheduler)
+    return scheduler
+
+
+@unittest.skipUnless(
+    _IS_APPLE_SILICON and torch.backends.mps.is_available(), _SKIP_REASON
+)
+class TestStashCrossDevice(unittest.TestCase):
+    """The FutureMap relay must live where the scheduler's batches live."""
+
+    @classmethod
+    def setUpClass(cls):
+        # init_overlap reads the exec config published with the server args.
+        set_global_server_args_for_scheduler(ServerArgs(model_path="dummy"))
+
+    def test_future_map_follows_req_pool_device(self):
+        scheduler = _init_overlap_mlx_scheduler(device="mps")
+
+        self.assertEqual(scheduler.future_map.output_tokens_buf.device.type, "cpu")
+
+    def test_stash_cpu_payload_batch(self):
+        """The MLX non-overlap combination: CPU tokens, mps scheduler, n>=2."""
+        scheduler = _init_overlap_mlx_scheduler(device="mps")
+        indices = torch.tensor([1, 2], dtype=torch.int64)
+        payload = RelayPayload(bonus_tokens=torch.tensor([101, 202], dtype=torch.int64))
+
+        scheduler.future_map.stash(indices, payload)
+
+        self.assertEqual(
+            scheduler.future_map.output_tokens_buf[indices].tolist(), [101, 202]
+        )
+
+    def test_stash_single_row(self):
+        """Sanity guard: the n == 1 path that already worked keeps working."""
+        scheduler = _init_overlap_mlx_scheduler(device="mps")
+        indices = torch.tensor([3], dtype=torch.int64)
+        payload = RelayPayload(bonus_tokens=torch.tensor([7], dtype=torch.int64))
+
+        scheduler.future_map.stash(indices, payload)
+
+        self.assertEqual(scheduler.future_map.output_tokens_buf[indices].tolist(), [7])
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()
